# Rain fell across part of the Atacama Desert in 2015 and again in 2017 after roughly five centuries without it, but instead of reviving the driest place on Earth, it wiped out as much as 87 percent of the microbial species living there Water shows up in one of the driest places on Earth, and the story writes itself\. Cracked ground drinks it in, dormant seeds swell, something long asleep stirs back to life\. We have all seen the time-lapse videos of a desert going green after a freak storm\. The intuition feels safe: rain in a place starved of it must be a gift\. In the driest core of the Atacama, that intuition was almost exactly backward\. The rain was not a rescue\. The researchers concluded that it killed most of the tiny life forms living in the flooded surface soils\. *A quick note on what this is\. We are not microbiologists or astrobiologists, and this is one field study of a rare event, not settled science about how life behaves everywhere\.
